title: I Used the Kayak-Rack Checkout on the Dockhand Who Skipped the Leash Log

parts.text: I signed kayak 4 at 9:08 a.m. and dockhand Ira launched without the leash line on the log. The board said: BOAT ON THE SHEET. LEASH CLIPPED. RETURN DRY. I was forty-one, renter, holding a card that listed 4. Ira shrugged. "Dockhands are the river." I photographed the board, the empty leash column, and the hull. Then I asked for the launch log. At 9:14 the harbor master pinged why Ira's name was on an unleashed hull. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The harbor master can see Ira's unleashed hull on the launch log during my checkout.

social.video_title: The dockhand launched without the leash column — Part 1/2
social.description: Kayak rack, an empty leash line, a board he posted. I logged the launch. Would you have asked for the harbor ping?

parts.text: Ira called it a quick put-in until the harbor master asked for the still. I printed the log, the board, and the photo. The leash clipped. Ira ran launches through the sheet like everyone else and told the next hand rivers were always about optics. Optics is a word dockhands use when a log exists. Checkout now has a second line: HANDS CLIP THE LEASH. I keep kayak 4 on a labeled slot. Ira brown-bags his jokes. The rack finally looks like a sheet, not a vibe. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Launch log, a clipped leash, and a second line. Was a quick put-in ever the river?
